decisions.reason: The hearty loaf is a low-cost extension of the core bread range on existing lines, and without a clear shortfall against aspirations there is little trigger to drop it, though bread assortments do rotate.

The mill tour leverages the heritage and event facilities central to the firm's experience positioning; post-pandemic recovery of visitor demand makes it worth carrying despite uncertain results, though some risk of discontinuation remains.
The sweet pastry is a cheap, close extension of the confectionery range with no evidence of underperformance that would prompt problemistic search.
The crusty farmhouse bread fits the traditional regional bread offer on existing production, so carrying it costs little and dropping it would bring few freed resources.
The gold-awarded poppy seed stollen is a flagship seasonal product whose results clearly exceed aspirations, so management has every reason to keep it.
The gold-awarded premium stollen performs above aspiration levels and strengthens the firm's festive quality reputation, making it a product to retain.
